title: Feature prompts and the visual loop
intro: Three features land on the RAG chatbot — and every prompt shares the same skeleton.

steps.title: The skeleton
steps.body:
Lesson 3's clickable-citations prompt, reduced to its bones:

- **Plan mode on** — approach reviewed before code.
- **@ anchors**: `@backend/document_processor.py`, `@backend/search_tools.py`.
- **Current behavior**: lesson links already live in the `course_catalog` collection.
- **Desired behavior**: each source becomes a clickable link opening the lesson in a new tab.
- **Constraints**: links embedded invisibly — no visible URL text.

steps.title: Iterate with eyes
steps.body:
The follow-up is a **pasted screenshot**: "these links are hard to read — make them more visually appealing." Visual work iterates on *images*, not adjectives.

The '+ New Chat' feature repeats the skeleton (clear conversation, new session without reload, cleanup on `@frontend` and `@backend`, match existing styling) — then closes the loop harder:

steps.title: Let Claude look for itself
steps.body: Attach the **Playwright MCP server** (`claude mcp add playwright npx @playwright/mcp@latest`, verify with `/mcp`) and the follow-up becomes: *"visit 127.0.0.1:8000 and view the '+ New Chat' button… left-aligned, border removed."*

points.label: Build
points.note: The feature lands from the skeleton prompt.

points.label: Look
points.note: Claude visits the running app through Playwright and takes its own screenshot.

points.label: Compare
points.note: Against your ask — alignment, borders, styling — and fixes what differs.

points.label: Permit
points.note: /permissions adds an allow rule by full tool name (mcp__playwright__browser_take_screenshot) so the loop runs unprompted.

steps.title: Features for the AI itself
steps.body:
Feature 3 adds a **new tool to the chatbot** — an outline tool returning exact lesson titles and links from the `course_metadata` collection. Claude Code can extend your AI system's own toolset — because the prompt explained the data it should build on.

> [!warn] The model is the muscle; the context is still the brain.

recap:
**Anchor files, state both behaviors, constrain the result, verify visually.**

- Plan mode + @files + current→desired + constraints = the skeleton.
- Screenshots and Playwright MCP close the loop with evidence, not adjectives.
- /permissions curates what runs unprompted, by full tool name.
- Well-fed prompts can extend your AI system's own tools.
